answer: Require every agent identity to stake a refundable bond locked for a full epoch and slashed if peers prove fraud, so spinning up thousands of fake identities costs real capital, not just keystrokes. A new identity starts in a nebula of untrusted newcomers with tiny transaction limits, and only earns wider access as independent counterparties attest to honest work over time, like a narrow inlet that widens gradually rather than a floodgate. The ivory-tower flaw of pure reputation scores is avoided because the bond, not votes, backs the claims.
